summary.intent: Plan wave-17 of the CipherBox v2.0.0 pre-cutover issue burndown: survey the 71 remaining open issues, resolve dependency/file-ownership lanes via recon agents, do housekeeping (orphaned issue parenting), get user decisions on scope-changing questions, and launch the first batch of ship agents.
summary.outcome: Housekeeping completed (11 orphan issues parented, #656/#990 umbrella states resolved), three recon agents produced a full lane plan, four scope decisions were made by the user (keep identity chain, ship full bin, land #1176 registry refcount, delete vestigial /auth/siwe/login), the #1399 bin work was decomposed into 6 filed sub-issues (#1552-#1557), and batch 1 (6 ship agents: F1, G, P, C, K, P1) was launched in isolated worktrees off commit 1df781d51, with 3 more lanes (P2, P4, I1) held back pending disk space.

repo: facade.rs (11708 lines) is the throughput ceiling for the engine: 14 of 32 open engine slices touch it, forcing a strictly serial merge chain rather than parallel lanes
GitHub sub-issues have a 100-child cap per parent — hit on umbrella #991, requiring reroute of overflow orphans to #635/#992

/auth/siwe/login is a vestigial dead route (only caller is engine Command::SiweLogin, no UI/e2e/desktop reference); wallet sign-in actually flows through the separate /auth/identity/wallet route used by WalletLoginButton.tsx and the e2e login page object
Lane A and Lane C both write write_plane.rs despite being scheduled 'parallel' — requires a simulated pairwise merge to avoid collision
PR #1550's WinFsp adapter set case_insensitive_lookup: true, turning previously pre-emptive issue #1539 into a live Windows trust-path bug
ADR-0010 supersedes the original #1399 proposal's bin-folder design (§6 table) in favor of an owner-sealed index — recon caught this before the decomposition was filed
zsh does not word-split loop variables the way bash does; a fetch loop over 53 issues silently stopped after one iteration until rewritten as a bash script file

code.finding: Still throws on REQUIRED_SHARE, locking out factor-policy members from desktop — #1268 cannot close by doc change alone, it's real engineering work
case_insensitive_lookup: true makes the node-id-order tiebreak (#1539) a live trust path on Windows, escalating its priority
Contains the highest-severity gap found in recon: a permanent unrecoverable third-party share lockout from a contact with no authority, must be fixed by #1345 part 2
Only remaining caller of /auth/siwe/login is Command::SiweLogin — confirms the route is safe to delete
Cited refusal removed by #1547, which is why #1430 was found stale during recon

workflow: Do orphan/housekeeping parenting before umbrella evaluation and wave planning — parent choice changes umbrella rollup counts that the plan reads

Recon agents should verify each candidate issue against the current main commit and report VALID/STALE/partly-landed status before lanes are trusted, since code drift between filing and planning is common

Ship agents run in isolated worktrees pinned to a single commit, each executing /simplify, /security-review, and crypto review where key material is touched, opening a draft PR and stopping at green CI — the orchestrator retains CodeRabbit resolution and merge control
A disk-space Monitor (alert under 15 GiB) is used to gate how many concurrent worktree-based ship agents can be launched at once

friction: zsh loop silently processed only 1 of 53 issues due to lack of word-splitting, requiring a rewrite as a bash script
GitHub's 100-sub-issue cap was hit unexpectedly on umbrella #991 mid-housekeeping, forcing a reroute of remaining orphans to alternate parents
Disk space constraints forced deferring 3 of 9 planned batch-1 lanes (P2, P4, I1) until other lanes free up or space allows
open_items: Launch deferred lanes P2 (#1268/#1428), P4 (#1380), and I1 (#1266) once disk space allows or a batch-1 lane finishes
#1430 to be closed as stale once P1 lands
#1507 verification and the #656 Grafana panel close to be folded into the #1390 cutover HITL step
Batch 4 (B5, B6, #1400, P9, P10) may roll into wave 18 given the facade chain's 8-serial-PR wall-clock limit
#857 to be closed via the finding folded into lane G rather than as a standalone fix
Full wave-17 plan targets ~24 PRs bringing open v2.0.0 issues from 71 down to roughly 15-20 by wave end
